**Description**
we are using [openebs/zfs ](https://github.com/openebs/zfs-localpv/blob/develop/deploy/zfs-operator.yaml) and we have multiple reports where users are having issues that boils down to the docker with zfs storage driver.

Pods are stuck in terminating state:
```
container <ID> driver "zfs" failed to remove root filesystem: exit status 1: "zfs fs destroy -r <dataset-path>" => cannot open '<dataset-path>': dataset does not exist"
```

Reports:
- https://jira.ixsystems.com/browse/NAS-112418
- https://www.truenas.com/community/threads/openebs-zfs-driver-removal-in-progress-for-4-weeks.96192/
- https://help.nextcloud.com/t/solved-cannot-start-service-db-error-creating-zfs-mount-after-zfs-snapshot-rollback/61695

This seems to have a workaround where you manually create missing datasets to make docker happy and things come back to normal.. which is tedious.

**Steps to reproduce the issue:**

comments: The `dataset does not exist` message is also mentioned in this thread: https://github.com/moby/moby/issues/40132

Hi have the same problem.

Can this case, where the ZFS volume to be deleted does not exists, be handled as a warning in the logs instead of a failure ?

## The details

A container is dead
```sh
$ docker ps -a | grep quizzical_kapitsa
CONTAINER ID   IMAGE                                      COMMAND                  CREATED             STATUS         PORTS               NAMES
e5d845b7f04d   7e652150d4f5                               "/bin/sh -c './confi…"   22 months ago       Dead                               quizzical_kapitsa
```

The creation date is strange as it was created by a **docker-compose build** a few minutes before.

Let's remove it
```sh
$ docker rm quizzical_kapitsa
Error response from daemon: container e5d845b7f04da595028ed461b9ee7ef1de351a2dcf3d55eab3fe35f89bbb05a4: driver "zfs" failed to remove root filesystem: exit status 1: "/usr/sbin/zfs destroy -r data0/docker/fcd1043c9b5b5e71f3afb7cf69e3a8efaaf31ba8b8a0b925fec317ac94a40445" => cannot open 'data0/docker/fcd1043c9b5b5e71f3afb7cf69e3a8efaaf31ba8b8a0b925fec317ac94a40445': dataset does not exist
```

The error from the docker daemon
```text
Sep 17 14:32:58 iota dockerd[26393]: time="2024-09-17T14:32:58.358043884Z" level=error msg="Handler for DELETE /v1.47/containers/quizzical_kapitsa returned error: container e5d845b7f04da595028ed461b9ee7ef1de351a2dcf3d55eab3fe35f89bbb05a4: driver \"zfs\" failed to remove root filesystem: exit status 1: \"/usr/sbin/zfs destroy -r data0/docker/fcd1043c9b5b5e71f3afb7cf69e3a8efaaf31ba8b8a0b925fec317ac94a40445\" => cannot open 'data0/docker/fcd1043c9b5b5e71f3afb7cf69e3a8efaaf31ba8b8a0b925fec317ac94a40445': dataset does not exist\n"
```

Let's recreate the ZFS volumes so docker can destroy them
```sh
root@iota:~# zfs create data0/docker/fcd1043c9b5b5e71f3afb7cf69e3a8efaaf31ba8b8a0b925fec317ac94a40445-init
root@iota:~# zfs create data0/docker/fcd1043c9b5b5e71f3afb7cf69e3a8efaaf31ba8b8a0b925fec317ac94a40445
```

And it worked
```sh
$ docker rm quizzical_kapitsa
quizzical_kapitsa
```

ZFS version: 2.2.6-1

I've ran into the same issue on a VPS (Ubuntu 22.04, zfs 2.1.5) which currently seems to suffer from a defect disk on the host machine (which lead to a high IO latency). Not realising this sooner, I've rebooted the system after a `docker system prune -f --volumes` had stalled (there were only a few untagged images on the system).

> Can this case, where the ZFS volume to be deleted does not exists, be handled as a warning in the logs instead of a failure ?

I second this, deleting a non-existent dataset should not be treated as an error. The missing dataset may be an anomaly, so logging a warning should suffice.

review_comments:
Did a quick rebase, and changed this to use `errors.As`;


```patch
diff --git a/daemon/graphdriver/zfs/zfs.go b/daemon/graphdriver/zfs/zfs.go
index bd96463d60..63301629af 100644
--- a/daemon/graphdriver/zfs/zfs.go
+++ b/daemon/graphdriver/zfs/zfs.go
@@ -4,6 +4,7 @@ package zfs // import "github.com/docker/docker/daemon/graphdriver/zfs"

 import (
        "context"
+       "errors"
        "fmt"
        "os"
        "os/exec"
@@ -362,7 +363,8 @@ func (d *Driver) Remove(id string) error {
        dataset := zfs.Dataset{Name: name}
        err := dataset.Destroy(zfs.DestroyRecursive)
        if err != nil {
-               errZfs, isZfsError := err.(*zfs.Error)
+               var errZfs *zfs.Error
+               isZfsError := errors.As(err, &errZfs)
                if isZfsError && strings.HasSuffix(errZfs.Stderr, "dataset does not exist\n") {
                        logger := log.G(context.TODO()).WithField("storage-driver", "zfs")
                        logger.WithError(err).Warnf("Tried to destroy inexistant dataset %q", name)
```
